Replayable Authority Histories for Auditing Automated Agents (https://www.ietf.org/ietf-ftp/internet-drafts/draft-rampertab-audit-agent-authority-history-00.html)
【turn768315view1】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; Content type: text/html; Source: open({"ref_id":"https://www.ietf.org/ietf-ftp/internet-drafts/draft-rampertab-audit-agent-authority-history-00.html","lineno":520}); Total lines: 1047
L455: Remote signers MAY take part through an encrypted ceremony that authenticates the parties, binds history, head, epoch, action and exact challenge, protects responses, and rejects expired, replayed or mismatched responses; it MUST provide the signer with the effect being approved and preserve uncertainty across retries. Transport encryption never replaces owner authorization, human eligibility or effect-boundary checks, and voucher participation in enrollment grants no owner vote.【308†¶】
L456: ### 【54†4.6.】 【55†Proof of Human Lineage attestation】
L457: 
L458: An instantiation MAY support a Proof of Human Lineage (PHL) attestation profile to decide which signing keys qualify as human-attested for a selected policy. The claim concerns the origin and assessment of a key's enrollment evidence, not authorship of content and not a guarantee that an agent will never use the key later. Biometric verification, key possession, identity, uniqueness, live presence and informed intent are distinct properties.【309†¶】
L459: A selected profile MUST define its biometric assurance, authenticator and verifier trust roots, exact-key binding, vouching requirements, bootstrap, validity and status rules, disclosure dependencies and a deterministic acceptance predicate. A generic user-verification result MUST NOT be described as biometric evidence when the mechanism also permits a PIN without distinguishing the method.
L460: WebAuthn [【310†WEBAUTHN3】] supplies useful authenticator evidence; attesting its credential does not attest a separate history-signing key. The proposed enrollment combines a method-qualified biometric ceremony, possession and explicit adoption of the exact signing key, and, for a remote subject, at least one other qualified human's signed vouch; the vouch MUST bind the same subject key, ceremony and assurance context, state what was observed, and be verifiable under the selected voucher trust policy.
L461: A circular chain of new vouches MUST NOT be accepted as a bootstrap. Verifiable credentials [【311†VC-DM2】] can carry claims; they do not establish their truth. An instantiation claiming replay enforcement MUST bind sufficient authenticated eligibility evidence into the replay input; a mutable registry lookup MUST NOT silently decide historical validity, and missing evidence MUST NOT silently qualify a key as human.
L462: Evidence MUST identify the key, profile, enrollment, issuer, voucher, time and status context and limitations; a profile MUST specify whether the verifier checks trusted admission statements or also revalidates their underlying evidence; missing required evidence MUST be reported as incomplete or unverified.【312†¶】
L463: Under the attested floor, a key's class is a function of the policy in force, its credential and the record's timestamp (【313†Table 10】). An attester is a party named in the policy in force.
L464: Its statement is a signed assertion bound to the exact credential, to the history's domain and, after the genesis, to the history's identity, with a validity interval; it is embedded in the policy and removed only by the owner quorum, never by the attester alone, and its subject MUST be an enrolled key or a committed next key not classed as an agent.【314†¶】
L465: 【315†Table 10】: 【316†Key classes under the attested floor】
L466: Class  | When  | May count toward
L467: --- | --- | ---
L468: HUMAN  | An attester's statement covers the record's time  | Everything the policy allows
L469: LAPSED  | The epoch's statement for the key has expired  | Only a record that reduces power by effect, a state checkpoint, or a restoration
L470: AGENT  | So classed by the policy  | Ordinary actions; never the floor, policy changes or rotations
L471: NONE  | Otherwise  | Nothing
L472: A restoration is a policy rotation that keeps every key, the commitment and every other field and only carries each statement as written or renews it; a renewal MUST name the same credential, MUST have started by the record's timestamp and after the epoch opened, and MUST extend the expiry.
L473: Lapse never removes a key: a carried expired statement MUST be kept through every rotation that keeps the key; a restoration MUST NOT add or remove a subject, and no subject's class may drop; a lapsed key never counts on a recovery rotation. A statement removed by the quorum is final.
L474: The policy MUST name at least two attesters; it MUST be refused when set unless at least a rotation quorum of its keys have valid statements and every lowered threshold is within the count of keys with started statements.【317†¶】
L475: The attested floor bounds history time: a control record whose counting signatures include at most one human-class credential MUST keep the preceding head's time or advance it no further than the attestation horizon, the latest expiry among the policy's statements, and MUST NOT reach the maximum representable time; two or more human-class signers MAY set any legal time. A committed next key MAY be attested before it is revealed; that is the only way a recovery signer counts as human.【318†¶】
L476: Three limits are stated and known not to hold: under the declared floor, class is a label; an attester's honesty and independence are not verified; and a key that can authorize a record alone chooses its timestamp, bounded only by the horizon under the attested floor and not at all under the declared one. Enrollment establishes a bounded prior association; a profile claiming fresh human approval of a particular action MUST bind a fresh biometric approval to the exact action challenge and displayed effect.
L477: Profiles MUST specify renewal, suspension and revocation, including the consequences of voucher or issuer misconduct, MUST distinguish historical acceptance under the committed evidence cutoff from current risk, and MUST keep later adverse evidence inspectable without rewriting yesterday's replay.
L478: A single key's head attestation MUST NOT be taken as proof of the human floor for its preceding history, and a head attestation signed by a lapsed, agent or unclassed key MUST NOT seed an abbreviated replay; nor may any single-key head attestation where the policy requires more than one signature for a checkpoint. A checkpoint recorded in the history under its own quorum MAY seed one.
L479: A profile supporting abbreviated replay MUST specify and validate an adequate starting-state authentication policy; otherwise full replay is required.【319†¶】
L480: ### 【56†4.7.】 【57†Capacity】
L481: A history MAY declare size limits. A declared limit MUST NOT refuse a control record that reduces power (revocation, epoch advance, termination, unappointment, witness unbinding). Absolute format or storage caps, unavailable durable storage or inability to sign may still prevent append; a history at an absolute terminal cap is extended by a successor history with its own genesis, which is distinct from same-case continuation (【240†Section 9】).
L482: A profile MUST define both operational and terminal limits and distinguish their failure reports.【320†¶】
L483: ## 【58†5.】 【59†Records and their verification】
L484: ### 【60†5.1.】 【61†The chain and the head】
L485: 
L486:       pos:   0         1         2               p
L487:            +-----+   +-----+   +-----+         +-----+
L488:            | gen |<--| r1  |<--| r2  |<-- ... <-| rp  |
L489:            +-----+   +-----+   +-----+         +-----+
L490:       hash  h0=H(0,gen) h1=H(h0,r1) h2=H(h1,r2)  hp=H(h(p-1),rp)
L491:       head at p = (hp, p, timestamp_p)
L492: 
L493: 
L494: 【321†Figure 4】: 【322†Each record commits to its predecessor; the head names a prefix】
L495: A conforming encoding MUST define a record hash at each position as a function of the previous hash and the record's content, under a collision-resistant hash with domain separation. The head at p is the triple (hash, position, timestamp), compared field by field.
L496: An edit, insertion or reordering changes every later hash; a fully rehashed substitute is detected only by a conflicting authenticated signature or held commitment, and removal of a complete suffix is not detectable from the chain alone (【190†Section 11.3】). A profile MUST distinguish internal consistency from authenticity.【323†¶】
L497: ### 【62†5.2.】 【63†Control signatures】
L498: 
L499: Every control record after the genesis MUST carry at least one valid owner signature and satisfy the selected approval policy. Each counting signature MUST be made by an admissible owner key (one in force at that position, or, on a recovery rotation, a committed key the rotation reveals with its possession proof) over a challenge that binds at least:【324†¶】
L500: 
L501:   * the history's domain, so the record cannot be replayed into another history;【325†¶】
L502:   * the record's identifier, type and timestamp;【326†¶】
L503: 
L504:   * the head before the record, so the record cannot be moved;【327†¶】
L505: 
L506:   * a hash of the record's effect, under profile-defined exclusions for the authorization containers themselves.【328†¶】
L507: A replay MUST reject a control record with absent, malformed, out-of-epoch or invalid required signatures, or whose eligible distinct signatures do not satisfy its effective policy. A multi-signature profile MUST define surplus, duplicate and ineligible entries and the exact container exclusions; an exclusion MUST NOT allow unsigned effect changes.
L508: Which threshold applies, and whether a record is a restoration or a recovery rotation, MUST be decided from the record, the signers' identifiers, the epoch record and the pre-event state alone, before any signature is verified, so the verdict never depends on verification order.【329†¶】
L509: ### 【64†5.3.】 【65†Session signatures】
L510: Every session record MUST carry a session binding and a type-specific signature. Profiles MUST specify exactly which bytes are authenticated; a generic claim that all envelopes are signed is insufficient. Records constructed after the final envelope is fixed SHOULD bind identifier, type, timestamp, preceding head, binding and effect.
L511: In the example encoding, declarations, refusals, effects, lifecycle events and counterparty wrappers bind their envelope; admissions instead sign the decision-time challenge (request, evaluation time, preceding head and session, role, intent and nonce bindings), and the admission's own identifier is committed by a later owner attestation. Migrated prefixes keep their source authorization.
L512: Session checks occur in each type's validation stage: find the session and credential, check the epoch fence, active agent, binding, expiry, challenge hash and signature. An admission additionally carries the authorization proof; replay MUST re-derive it from the pre-admission state and recorded inputs and require canonical byte equality. A missing or mismatched credential is not a fence failure.【330†¶】
L513: ### 【66†5.4.】 【67†Replay and determinism】
L514: A reader reconstructs state by replaying every record from genesis under the profile's fixed check order; the profile MUST specify chain, schema, authorization, transition and capacity precedence. A rejected record leaves the state unchanged, the rejection names the position, and a history containing a rejected record is invalid as a whole.
L515: Given the same history, request and evaluation time, every conforming implementation MUST produce the same decision, proof and evidence list; evaluation time is an explicit input, never the reader's clock, and evidence lists MUST be ordered deterministically. A specification instantiating this model SHOULD publish conformance vectors and SHOULD have at least two independent implementations pass them; passing a finite set is bounded evidence, not universal correctness.【331†¶】
L516: ### 【68†5.5.】 【69†Evidence references】
L517: Every claim a decision or query makes MUST be supported by an evidence reference naming a record by identifier, type, position and history hash. Further kinds MAY name an authority by its grant record, a credential by its admission, a receipt by content hash and record, or an external attestation by type, reference and attester. Evidence is bounded; a result whose evidence would exceed the bound is INDETERMINATE with an explicit code, never silently truncated.【332†¶】
L518: ### 【70†5.6.】 【71†State commitment】
L519: A conforming encoding MUST define a state root committing to the complete set of state records at a position, such that matching roots commit to matching record sets. Inclusion needs a verified path, leaf index and tree size; sorted non-membership additionally needs authenticated adjacent indices and boundary proofs and an authenticated commitment whose ordering and uniqueness were validated; two arbitrary inclusion paths are insufficient.
L520: A Merkle tree over the sorted state records in the manner of [【215†RFC6962】] satisfies this. An instantiation MUST support owner-signed checkpoints and root-bearing head attestations, distinguishing the state before a checkpoint from the state including it. A reader resuming from a cache MUST recompute the root and compare it with an owner-signed root at exactly that position, falling back to full replay on mismatch; a mismatch alone does not establish owner-key misuse.
L521: A signed starting state is an owner assertion unless independently replayed.【333†¶】
L522: ## 【72†6.】 【73†Decisions and refusals】
L523: ### 【74†6.1.】 【75†The decision procedure】
L524: 
L525: A request names an actor, an action, a resource and a claimed time, and optionally an amount, a counterparty and a commitment to terms. A decision is one of the results in 【334†Table 11】.【335†¶】
L526: 【336†Table 11】: 【337†The three decision results】
L527: Result  | Meaning  | Carries
L528: --- | --- | ---
L529: ALLOW  | Authority exists  | A proof: the root, the permission path from root to actor, intersections satisfied, effective constraints after attenuation, the controlling authority identifiers, usage snapshot of every capped grant, authority evidence, prohibitions checked
L530: DENY  | Authority does not exist or is overridden  | A code and a sorted list of failures with evidence. Codes MUST at least distinguish: action not allowed, no authority, revoked, expired, not yet valid, prohibited, agent inactive, session fenced, missing intersection, amount exceeded
L531: INDETERMINATE  | The history or request cannot support a decision (unverifiable relation, invalid causal time, evidence over the bound)  | A code and evidence. MUST NOT be treated as ALLOW; an enforcement point that must choose MUST treat it as a refusal
L532: The procedure MUST evaluate, in order: domain and policy identifiers; causal time (evaluation time not before the head's time); the actor's lifecycle; the session binding when the request is consequential; candidate permission paths from recognized roots; delegation status along each path; required intersections; prohibitions; per-grant limits including cumulative usage. Budgets (【259†Section 6.3】) are consulted only after an ALLOW and can only turn it into a DENY.
L533: Every result MUST state, as constant values, that it is a reading of the captured history and not a capability to execute anything.【338†¶】
L534: ### 【76†6.2.】 【77†Consequential requests and admissions】
L535: A request intended for consequential execution is consequential. The runtime declares an intent (actor, action, resource, role and tenure, the adapter that will carry it out, optional amount, counterparty and terms commitment, and a nonce); the engine records an admission carrying the evaluation time, the expected head and the proof.
L536: After an admission the record may show a consumption (the adapter's signed acknowledgment), an outcome (confirmed, failed, disputed or unknown), a receipt (a compact artifact checkable against a supplied prefix), and effects (measurements reported by a session, connector or counterparty). None establishes that the world changed; each establishes that a signer claimed something at a head.
L537: A job with an uncertain submission stays outcome-unknown until reconciled; exactly-once effects require executor idempotency and recovery, which a signed history cannot supply by itself.【339†¶】
L538: ### 【78†6.3.】 【79†Budgets】
L539: 
L540: An instantiation MUST support budgets: owner-declared stop rules over a group of requests selected by actors, roles, actions, resources and metric, with a cap per period, per operation or in count, and bounded carry-over. A budget selected by role MUST follow the role across a handover. Budgets are charged by admissions only, never by refusals or effects; a matching selector alone does not meter effects.【340†¶】
L541: ### 【80†6.4.】 【81†Refusals as records】
L542: 
L543: A conforming history MUST support a refusal record, session-signed, with the fields in 【341†Table 12】.【342†¶】
L544: 【343†Table 12】: 【344†The refusal record】
L545: Field  | Rule
L546: --- | ---
L547: Source  | The authority procedure (CORE), a budget, or a connector (an enforcement point outside the engine)
L548: Request  | As evaluated
L549: Evaluation time  | MUST equal the record's timestamp
L550: Expected head  | MUST be the head immediately before the record
L551: Decision and code  | DENY or INDETERMINATE; the budget identifier for a budget refusal; connector identifier, code and detail digest for a connector refusal
L552: Signer  | For CORE and budget refusals the signing session's agent MUST be the request's actor; for a connector refusal, the connector's own admitted agent
L553: For CORE and budget refusals, replay MUST re-run the decision on the state before the record and MUST reject the record unless decision, code and budget identifier are reproduced; a refusal the state would have allowed is a replay rejection. A connector refusal is attested, not re-derived: the engine cannot reproduce a decision it did not make.
L554: A reproduced DENY establishes the recorded denial at that head; INDETERMINATE establishes that the inputs could not support ALLOW; an attested refusal proves only that an admitted connector claimed to have refused. An expired, fenced, terminated or never-admitted actor cannot sign its own CORE or budget refusal; a live connector session can attest the mapped attempt instead.【345†¶】
L555: Refusals never change usage counters. A writer SHOULD coalesce identical refusals per actor within a short window and SHOULD rate-limit them, and MUST report whether a refusal was recorded and, if not, why; the history therefore need not enumerate every attempt. A deployment that wants refusals enforced as well as recorded MUST place the decision point where the action is executed (【346†Section 10.1】).【347†¶】
L556: ## 【82†7.】 【83†Counterparty receipts and external policy】
L557: ### 【84†7.1.】 【85†Counterparty receipts】
L558: An instantiation MUST support owner-authorized registration and retirement of counterparty verification keys and session-recorded counterparty receipts, distinguishing a local issuer receipt, a commitment to an artifact, and a separately counterparty-signed artifact; a digest alone MUST NOT be reported as authenticated counterparty evidence.
L559: A receipt MUST bind the history identity, counterparty and key, the earlier admitted intent and its declaration digest, and the reported effect and time; its wrapper MUST bind the recording session and preceding head. Replay MUST require an ACTIVE counterparty with the named key at the wrapper position and verify the envelope signature before the wrapper authorization. Retirement MUST NOT invalidate an earlier accepted wrapper; new wrappers during retirement MUST be rejected.
L560: Re-registration may replace keys while preserving the receipt chain; a credential replaced this way leaves the history's records and the one-job rule (【241†Section 4.5】) can no longer see it. A profile MUST specify uniqueness, duplicate and reference-ordering rules and the consistency of duplicated receipt and effect fields; a wrapper referencing an earlier envelope MUST carry or reference it so an exporter can supply the dependency.
L561: Verification MUST report artifact authenticity, historical authority, canonical inclusion and current usability separately. A counterparty's signature establishes its claim, not settlement, delivery or legal effect.【348†¶】
L562: ### 【86†7.2.】 【87†External policy composition】
L563: An instantiation MUST support composition with an application-selected external decider (Cedar and OpenFGA are examples) through a profile-defined interface. The application MUST bind both decisions to the same captured actor, action, resource, arguments or their commitment, and contextual inputs.
L564: For a required external policy, the broker MUST admit a new effect only when the model returns ALLOW and the decider returns an authenticated, supported ALLOW under the configured policy identity; denial, error, missing evidence and an unavailable required decider MUST prevent dispatch. An external ALLOW MUST NOT override a model denial or create a grant, duty discharge or succession power.
L565: The profile MUST identify policy, model and store versions, input provenance, freshness, error handling and restart behavior, and MUST distinguish a pinned policy model from mutable relationship data. The application MUST durably retain the external result before admission and link it to the captured request, and MUST recheck current history, authority and clock after asynchronous evaluation or signing.
L566: Post-admission external-policy liveness MUST be checked at the executor boundary or the enforcement claim refused; a profile MUST NOT advertise cross-service atomicity merely because both decisions allowed at admission.【349†¶】
L567: ## 【88†8.】 【89†Duties, handover and lineage】
L568: ### 【90†8.1.】 【91†Duties】
L569: An instantiation MUST support durable obligations and attempt duties with signed creation, assignment and status records. A duty is created from a recorded operation and its receipt, by an administrative session record, and carries its identifier, source intent, causal receipt, durable role, tenure, description, deadline, status, beneficiary, terms commitment, current performance assignee, optional succession rule and transition policies.
L570: Statuses are OPEN, OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, DISPUTED, DISCHARGED and IMPOSSIBLE_OR_ESCALATED; a status change and a performance assignment are each signed administrative records. An attempt duty preserves follow-up responsibility for an uncertain operation; a profile MUST distinguish its creation rules, and an investigation review MUST NOT be interpreted as fulfillment or automatic discharge.【350†¶】
L571: ### 【92†8.2.】 【93†Succession and handover】
L572: 
L573: When a predecessor is terminated under a succession rule, the writer MUST provide a specified atomic handover operation; profiles MUST define crash recovery and the visibility of intermediate prefixes, since two adjacent valid events alone do not prove atomic storage. 【351†Table 13】 states what MUST hold across a handover.【352†¶】
L574: 【353†Table 13】: 【354†Handover rules】
L575: What  | Across a handover
L576: --- | ---
L577: Open duties under the applied rule  | Belong to the role; stay OPEN and are reported as surviving until the successor records a signed performance assignment
L578: Grants  | Do not follow. The report MUST list every live grant of the predecessor, each marked as not following
L579: Delegations the predecessor issued  | Evaluated against the predecessor's status; after termination they yield no ALLOW
L580: Budgets selected by the role  | Follow the role
L581: The predecessor's sessions  | Cease to authorize requests while the agent is inactive; credentials are not deleted and the epoch is not advanced
L582: ### 【94†8.3.】 【95†Queries】
L583: 
L584: A conforming instantiation MUST support the queries in 【355†Table 14】, each answered from the captured history with evidence references and an explicit epistemic status: established from a verified replay, or not established and why.【356†¶】
L585: 【357†Table 14】: 【358†The four queries】
L586: Query  | Answers
L587: --- | ---
L588: WHY  | For a request: which grants, in which order, under which constraints, from which root, in which session and tenure
L589: RESPONSIBLE  | For an action: who is attributable at the time (actor, session, role, principal, mandator, authority source, controller) and who holds the duty afterwards. A statement about the records, not a legal judgment
L590: SURVIVES  | For an agent: lifecycle status, tenures, duties that outlive it, assignments, unresolved intents, reported outcomes, and authority dependencies its termination invalidates
L591: LINEAGE  | For an authority, admission or request: the capability roots and grant paths that support it, including required intersections and issuance authorizations, with any established human-lineage assessment. Confers no permission
L592: ### 【96†8.4.】 【97†Proof of Human Lineage】
L593: A PHL lineage query verifies recorded authority lineage and stated human-evidence predicates under selected policies. It MUST identify its selector, authenticated history identity, evaluated head and time, interpretation and assessment policies, disclosure scope and path-selection rule; an admission query MUST use the replay-reproduced decision path with all required intersections.
L594: The capability root is the root permission a path descends from; it is distinct from the history owner, the owner keys in force at the root-grant event and the grantor named there, and an answer MUST identify these separately. A valid owner signature on a grant establishes the recorded edge; it MUST NOT by itself be reported as human evidence for the grantor or grantee.【359†¶】
L595: For a root issued under several owner approvals the answer MUST distinguish (a) whether its actual counting quorum contains a qualifying human-attested credential, (b) whether every quorum permitted by its policy requires one, and (c) any assessment of the named grantor; "human-authorized capability root issuance" denotes (a), judged in the root-grant event's frozen context. Counting MUST use the policy in force before the event.
L596: A query MUST distinguish established-true, established-false and unknown; missing or withheld evidence MUST NOT be treated as non-human; verification MUST terminate within declared limits and report partial coverage; and for several roots the answer MUST name its quantifier and MUST distinguish alternative paths from required partner paths. An authority-only query MUST distinguish provenance and liveness from action-specific authorization, and each returned path MUST keep its own root and result.
L597: Per-edge assessments MUST carry evidence references and MUST distinguish assessment at the edge's event, at query time and as current risk; under the attested floor a lapsed class MUST be reported as lapsed, and later expiry or revocation MUST NOT silently rewrite an established event-time conclusion. An unknown required branch prevents an established-true all-required-roots conclusion; an established-false required branch can establish a false one despite another unknown branch.
L598: A limited or redacted view MUST NOT assert an exhaustive all-path or total-count conclusion. Invalid supplied evidence MUST be distinguished from evidence unavailability. Ordinary authority validity and PHL attestation assurance MUST be reported separately unless the selected authority profile makes the latter an acceptance condition.
L599: A human signature in one observed quorum MUST NOT establish proposition (b); a genesis key set MUST NOT be presented as an inferred root-grant signing quorum; actor binding MUST NOT be counted as an owner approval.
L600: Counts MUST state their unit, deduplicate exact credentials, exclude evidence-only vouchers (a human-associated credential count MUST include only credentials whose assessment is established and report counting-authorization and actor-binding sets separately, and a count under a uniqueness policy MUST name that policy's domain, issuer assumptions and incomplete coverage), and MUST NOT present distinct keys as distinct humans; absent an authenticated uniqueness policy, a distinct-human count is reported as not established.
L601: A declared HUMAN class or omitted-class default MUST NOT be reported as a verified assessment. Disclosure MAY hide identities through a reviewed selective-disclosure profile whose public proof binds the same predicate, scope and context.【360†¶】
L602: ### 【98†8.5.】 【99†Query scope and investigation】
L603: A query result MUST bind the exact domain, genesis identity, interpretation versions, disclosure scope, evaluated head and time, and MUST distinguish a replay-derived conclusion from unavailable evidence, unsupported interpretation or unverified freshness; missing evidence MUST NOT be relabeled as DENY, and a caller-supplied proof or serialized state MUST NOT acquire established status from matching metadata alone.
L604: A query about an earlier prefix MUST report whether the supplied history's head is the same prefix, a verified strict extension (later position and matching commitment) or unverified. A historical ALLOW remains an answer about that prefix; present consequential use requires a separate current authorization. Commitment integrity, inclusion, finality, availability, historical authorization, freshness and external outcome MUST be reported as distinct axes.
L605: A private or commitment-only deployment MUST NOT claim a publicly reconstructible undisclosed graph. Public reconstruction MUST require independently obtainable bodies, schemas, policies and opening material; an unexplained root alone is insufficient. An indexer, cache or explanation interface MUST NOT be accepted as an authority source because it displays the records.【361†¶】
L606: An instantiation MUST support a prospective, duty-scoped investigation policy, an authorized evidence-bound disposition and a durable contest. Activation MUST identify one existing duty, its rules commitment, the activating actor and the prior head, and MUST NOT rewrite earlier meanings or grant general upgrade power; the profile MUST specify one-activation and compatibility rules, signer purposes, authority prerequisites and finite disposition and contest allowances.
L607: A disposition MUST distinguish the attester's signed finding from the performer's authorization to record it; replay MUST check each purpose-bound signature, role and session binding, authority and exact evidence commitment; the same actor MAY fill both roles only if both powers and both signature purposes are checked; the writer MUST re-evaluate fresh eligibility of both after each asynchronous signature and again under the writer lock, with the head unchanged, fresh time at or after the signed time and both authority routes unchanged, without altering signed challenges.
L608: Assignment, a restored resource, a reported APPLIED outcome or a reviewed report MUST NOT alone close the duty. The duty view MUST distinguish OPEN, COMPLETED_UNDER_POLICY, ESCALATED, NEEDS_REVIEW and CONTESTED, keep the original creation status, apply the profile's review-freshness rule on new evidence or assignment, and report accepted contests until an explicit adjudication resolves them.
L609: Completion under a local policy MUST NOT be reported as external proof or legal discharge, and old readers MUST return an explicit unsupported result rather than a misleading status.【362†¶】
L610: ## 【100†9.】 【101†Execution recovery and continuation】
L611: ### 【102†9.1.】 【103†Admission, dispatch and uncertain outcomes】
L612: An instantiation MUST support distinct intent, admission, submission attempt, consumption, outcome, observation and receipt states. A configured executor profile MUST bind target identity, schema and version, captured arguments, enforcement mode, business identity and idempotency identity before signing the intent; untrusted request data MUST NOT select callbacks, credentials or destinations outside the configured profile.【363†¶】
L613: 
L614:       intent --> admission --> [submit] --> consumption --> outcome
L615:                                   |                          |
L616:                                   | timeout / crash          | unknown
L617:                                   v                          v
L618:                        keep original identity,      reconcile via status
L619:                        reserved allowance,          and evidence route;
L620:                        outcome UNKNOWN              never re-dispatch on
L621:                                                     an empty lookup
L622: 【364†Figure 5】: 【365†An uncertain submission keeps its identity; it is never silently repeated】
L623: A broker MUST durably record the admitted submission identity before sending. After a timeout, lost response or crash it MUST preserve the original identity, reserved allowance and unknown outcome, MUST NOT dispatch again merely because a lookup is empty, and MUST recover through the original identity and a status or evidence route.
L624: A new operation, compensation or restoration MUST obtain its own current authority; a late report MUST be recorded as evidence under current recording authority without manufacturing a receipt, releasing allowance or granting execution permission. The profile MUST state its rollback, full-state-loss and host-trust limitations.
L625: A cooperating destination MUST authenticate the coordinator, accept checkpoints only as exact history extensions, durably acknowledge the effective fence and recheck the admission's control tuple and required authority liveness, under the declared time and policy assumptions, at its commit boundary; cancellation and application MUST share the profile's durable ordering boundary; a cancellation after APPLIED MUST be reported as too late; staging a new checkpoint MUST NOT be reported as an acknowledged fence.
L626: Atomic effect-and-idempotency commitment MUST be one durable transaction; missing or corrupt restart state MUST fail closed and MUST NOT silently reinitialize a destination; retention of attempt identities and tombstones MUST be bounded and MUST refuse growth rather than forget replay protection.【366†¶】
L627: ### 【104†9.2.】 【105†Same-case continuation】
L628: An instantiation MUST provide an explicit continuation mechanism. A same-case storage profile MUST preserve the original domain and genesis, canonical bytes and global positions, interpretation versions, signatures, usage, revocations, nonce state, reservations, attempts and open duties; a suffix-only replay or a fresh genesis MUST NOT be represented as a continuation.
L629: A segmented profile MUST reconstruct from genesis or an authenticated starting state, commit immutable segments before publishing their manifest, acknowledge only after the required durable barriers, and reconcile uncertain writes against the committed manifest; conditional append MUST check the storage generation and canonical head under an exclusive writer boundary, and orphan data MUST NOT silently become canonical or cause fallback to an older head.
L630: Migration MUST be explicit, preserve the originals and existing attempts, usage, identities and capacity obligations, verify the source and prevent concurrent use of the old write path; destination transfer MUST independently validate the transferred complete history before acknowledging its checkpoint; an exact same-history retry MUST preserve the original durable result and MUST NOT create another effect or reset allowance.
L631: A storage manifest is integrity evidence under host assumptions, not finality.【367†¶】
L632: ### 【106†9.3.】 【107†Interfaces and service boundaries】
L633: An instantiation MUST expose separate read-only inspection, authorization evaluation and controlled write interfaces. CLI, SDK, Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent-framework bindings are application interfaces, not authority sources; an authenticated caller binding MUST map a connection to the configured actor, session and tenure; untrusted caller parameters MUST NOT select another actor's privilege; and read-only handles MUST NOT become execution capabilities.
L634: A protected-resource profile MUST identify the trusted host, custody and access boundary; restoration requires separate authorization and MUST NOT discharge the investigation duty. A service MUST bound its resources, capture one consistent observation per composite query and apply an explicit disclosure policy; a natural-language explanation interface MUST retain the typed result and evidence links and MUST NOT upgrade an unverified conclusion.
L635: A durable-job interface MUST persist an opaque handle bound to the original attempt before launch, check caller access and permission on every poll, inspection or cancellation, and MUST NOT infer an effect retry from reconnection; a handle MUST NOT confer authority, and a cancellation acknowledgment MUST distinguish stopping later outgoing phases from cancellation at the destination and from rollback of an applied effect.
L636: An authenticated HTTP binding MUST validate issuer, audience, token type and lifetime, MUST reject token-supplied discovery keys or URLs outside the configured trust policy, MUST NOT forward bearer credentials upstream or retain them in records, MUST recheck caller access around asynchronous signing, dispatch and disclosure, and MUST NOT interpret a disconnect, expired token or refusal as cancellation or proof of no effect. A public service profile MUST specify HTTPS and custody boundaries.
L637: Access loss after an effect MUST preserve the attempt while withholding disclosure under current policy.【368†¶】
L638: ## 【108†10.】 【109†Reconciliation】
L639: ### 【110†10.1.】 【111†Why a decision point is not enough】
L640: No decision point sees every call: a host may execute a tool without asking, a sub-agent may run without the hook, a script may call a service directly, and a token the agent holds may be used outside any gate. A history that records only what passed through the decision point proves what the decision point saw and decided, not what the agent did.

A claim that an agent is "governed" without this table is not supported by the model.【370†¶】
